assignedReviews.card_evidence: A hormone is barely a tiny amount in your blood, yet it affects your whole body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Hormone potency is endocrine trivia, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it affects your whole body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Hormone amount is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en: A hormone is barely a tiny amount in your blood, yet it affects your whole body — like a pinch of salt changing the taste of an entire dish.
copy.tl: Napakakaunti lang ng hormone sa dugo, pero malaki ang epekto nito sa buong katawan — parang kaunting asin na nagbabago ng lasa ng buong ulam.
copy.bis: Gamay ra kaayo ang hormone sa dugo, apan dako ang epekto niini sa tibuok lawas — sama sa gamay nga asin nga makausab sa lami sa tibuok sud-an.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists call warm-blooded animals 'endothermic' and cold-blooded animals 'ectothermic'.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a classification of animals by body temperature regulation, but the competency requires using a table to classify living things into the named groups (plants flowering/non-flowering; animals mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms fungi/bacteria). The card does not use a table and does not address the specified groups or characteristics.

copy.en:
What do scientists call warm-blooded animals?

Scientists call warm-blooded animals 'endothermic' and cold-blooded animals 'ectothermic'.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag ng mga siyentipiko sa mainit-dugo?

Tinatawag ng mga siyentipiko na 'endothermic' ang mga hayop na mainit ang dugo, at 'ectothermic' ang malamig ang dugo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tawag sa siyentista sa mainiton og dugo?

Gitawag sa mga siyentista og 'endothermic' ang mainiton og dugo, ug 'ectothermic' ang bugnaw og dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: some of that energy is lost as heat into the environment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that work is done when a force causes the displacement of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy loss as heat during life processes, but the competency requires recognizing that work is done when a force causes displacement. The card does not mention force, displacement, or work, so it only shares the broad topic of energy and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Organisms use energy for life processes like breathing, moving, and digesting food, and some of that energy is lost as heat into the environment.
copy.tl: Ginagamit ng mga organismo ang energy para sa mga life process tulad ng paghinga, paggalaw, at pagtunaw ng pagkain, at ang ilan sa energy na iyon ay nawawala bilang init sa kapaligiran.
copy.bis: Gigamit sa mga organismo ang energy alang sa mga life process sama sa pagginhawa, paglihok, ug paghilis sa pagkaon, ug ang uban niana nga energy mawala isip init sa palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes from one form into another!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity, such as when objects fall
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the general principle of conservation of energy but does not describe it in everyday situations involving gravity, such as objects falling, as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes from one form into another!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions energy changing form but provides no examples of kinetic energy transforming to potential energy or vice versa, so it does not directly support identifying such everyday situations.

copy.en: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes from one form into another!
copy.tl: Ang enerhiya ay hindi nalilikha ni nawawala, nagbabago lang ito ng anyo patungo sa iba!
copy.bis: Ang enerhiya dili mahimo o mawala, mausab lamang kini gikan sa usa ka porma ngadto sa lain!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines is one of the world's largest producers of geothermal energy because of its many volcanoes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions geothermal energy production in the Philippines but does not evaluate how renewable/non-renewable electricity generation impacts human activities or the environment, which is the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines is one of the world's largest producers of geothermal energy because of its many volcanoes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card links volcanoes to geothermal energy but does not identify locations of active/inactive volcanoes or assess eruption risk to a local community, as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines is one of the world's largest producers of geothermal energy because of its many volcanoes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions volcanoes as a landform but does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water or describe their influence on living and non-living components, which is the focus of the competency.

copy.en:
Why is the Philippines a top producer of geothermal energy?

The Philippines is one of the world's largest producers of geothermal energy because of its many volcanoes!
copy.tl:
Bakit ang Pilipinas ay isa sa pinakamalaking gumagawa ng geothermal energy?

Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa pinakamalaking gumagawa ng geothermal energy sa buong mundo dahil sa dami ng mga bulkan nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong ang Pilipinas usa sa pinakadako nga naghimog geothermal energy?

Ang Pilipinas usa sa pinakadako nga naghimog geothermal energy sa tibuok kalibotan tungod sa daghan niini nga mga bulkan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sun is the main source of nearly all the energy we use right here on Earth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the Sun is the main source of energy on Earth. It does not describe any overall characteristics of the Sun such as its composition, size, or the specific main energy it radiates (e.g., light and heat). The statement is a general claim about the Sun's role, not a description of the Sun's characteristics required by the competency.

copy.en:
Where does almost all our energy come from?

The sun is the main source of nearly all the energy we use right here on Earth!
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang halos lahat ng enerhiya natin?

Ang araw ang pangunahing pinagkukunan ng halos lahat ng enerhiyang ginagamit natin dito sa Mundo!
copy.bis:
Asa galing ang hapit tanang enerhiya nato?

Ang adlaw mao ang nag-unang tinubdan sa hapit tanang enerhiya nga atong gigamit dinhi sa Kalibotan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is named after the scientist James Joule.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card names James Joule as a scientist, but it does not identify an invention or describe his scientific work. The joule is a unit, not an invention, so the card does not directly support identifying a scientist and their invention/s.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The SI unit of energy and work is the joule (J)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that work is done when a force causes the displacement of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that the joule is the SI unit of energy and work, but it does not explain that work is done when a force causes displacement of an object. It only names the unit, so it does not directly teach the concept of work in the competency.

copy.en: The SI unit of energy and work is the joule (J)! It is named after the scientist James Joule.
copy.tl: Ang SI unit ng enerhiya at trabaho (work) ay joule (J)! Ipinangalan ito sa siyentipikong si James Joule.
copy.bis: Ang SI unit sa enerhiya ug trabaho (work) kay joule (J)! Ginganlan kini sa siyentipiko nga si James Joule.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In mung bean, the seed leaves rise above the soil when it sprouts; in corn, they stay buried underground.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific germination detail (cotyledon position) but does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants from seed to mature plant. It does not directly support the competency's comparative life-cycle skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In mung bean, the seed leaves rise above the soil when it sprouts; in corn, they stay buried underground.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions seed leaves (cotyledons) but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important. It is only tangentially related to plant structures.

copy.en: In mung bean, the seed leaves rise above the soil when it sprouts; in corn, they stay buried underground.
copy.tl: Sa mungo, umaahon sa ibabaw ng lupa ang mga dahon ng binhi kapag tumubo; sa mais, nananatili itong nasa ilalim ng lupa.
copy.bis: Sa mongo, mosaka sa ibabaw sa yuta ang mga dahon sa liso kon motubo na; sa mais, nagpabilin kini sa ilalom sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An epiphyte's roots never reach the ground. Instead, they cling to tree bark or to cracks in the branches.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes where epiphyte (aerial) roots are located and what they cling to, but does not describe the purpose or function of the specialized structure. The competency requires describing the purpose of specialized structures such as aerial roots; the card only states their placement, not their role (e.g., absorbing moisture, anchoring).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An epiphyte's roots never reach the ground. Instead, they cling to tree bark or to cracks in the branches.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots but does not address the role of roots in getting water and nutrients from the soil. In fact, it states the roots do not reach the ground, which is contrary to the competency's focus on roots obtaining water and nutrients from soil. It provides no support for observing outer plant parts and identifying their role in soil-based water/nutrient uptake.

copy.en:
Where do an epiphyte's roots go if not into the ground?

An epiphyte's roots never reach the ground. Instead, they cling to tree bark or to cracks in the branches.
copy.tl:
Saan pumupunta ang ugat ng epiphyte kung hindi sa lupa?

Ang ugat ng epiphyte ay hindi umaabot sa lupa. Sa halip, kumakapit ito sa balat ng puno o sa mga siwang ng sanga.
copy.bis:
Asa moadto ang gamot sa epiphyte kon dili sa yuta?

Ang gamot sa epiphyte dili moabot sa yuta. Hinuon, mokapit kini sa panit sa kahoy o sa mga liki sa sanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it clings to trees and catches water and rotting leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an epiphytic habit and leaf shape but does not name or explain a specific specialized structure such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots, nor does it clearly describe the purpose of a specialized structure.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: catches water and rotting leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions catching water and rotting leaves, which relates to obtaining resources, but it does not explain adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: leaves shaped like deer antlers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves but does not describe their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil; the epiphyte's water capture is from air and debris, not soil.

copy.en:
What is a staghorn fern?

The staghorn fern is an epiphyte with leaves shaped like deer antlers — it clings to trees and catches water and rotting leaves!
copy.tl:
Ano ang staghorn fern?

Ang staghorn fern ay isang epiphyte na may dahong hugis-sungay ng usa — kumakapit ito sa puno at nakukuha ang tubig at nabubulok na dahon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang staghorn fern?

Ang staghorn fern usa ka epiphyte nga adunay dahon nga porma sa sungay sa usa — mokapit kini sa kahoy ug makakuha og tubig ug nadunot nga dahon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are two (2) equinoxes each year: the March equinox and the September equinox!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain, using models, how the tilt of the Earth affects the changes in the length of daytime at different times of the year
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that there are two equinoxes per year. It does not mention Earth's tilt, daytime length, or use models, so it does not directly support explaining how tilt affects changes in daytime length.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are two (2) equinoxes each year: the March equinox and the September equinox!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions equinoxes, which are related to seasonal patterns, but it does not involve a Sun-Earth-Moon model, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses, and it does not demonstrate or explain any observable effect.

copy.en: There are two (2) equinoxes each year: the March equinox and the September equinox!
copy.tl: May dalawang (2) equinox bawat taon: ang March equinox at ang September equinox!
copy.bis: Adunay duha (2) ka equinox matag tuig: ang March equinox ug ang September equinox!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rain, wind, and water slowly wear them down in a process called erosion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes erosion as a wearing-down process but does not demonstrate or explain how erosion transports Earth materials, which is the specific action of the competency.

copy.en: While mountains rise, rain, wind, and water slowly wear them down in a process called erosion!
copy.tl: Habang tumataas ang mga bundok, dahan-dahan silang naaagnas ng ulan, hangin, at tubig sa proseso ng erosion!
copy.bis: Samtang nagtaas ang mga bukid, hinay-hinay sad silang nakaykay sa ulan, hangin, ug tubig sa proseso nga gitawag og erosion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An escalator is a moving staircase! Its steps are attached to a long chain that loops around and around, all driven by a motor.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how an escalator works, but an escalator is a complex machine, not a simple machine. The competency G6-F-1 specifically targets simple machines found at home, school, and community. The card does not describe any simple machine or its use, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: An escalator is a moving staircase! Its steps are attached to a long chain that loops around and around, all driven by a motor.
copy.tl: Ang escalator ay isang gumagalaw na hagdan! Ang mga baitang nito ay nakakabit sa isang mahabang kadena na umiikot nang paulit-ulit, pinapaandar ng motor.
copy.bis: Ang escalator usa ka naglihok nga hagdanan! Ang mga baitang niini nasumpay sa taas nga kadena nga magtuyok balik-balik, gipadagan sa usa ka motor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Muscles in your esophagus squeeze food along in wave-like motions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes peristalsis in the esophagus, which is part of digestive tract movement, but the competency requires a labeled diagram tracing food through the digestive tract and explaining specific digestive processes (mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, elimination). No diagram is used, and peristalsis is not one of the listed processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Muscles in your esophagus squeeze food along in wave-like motions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the esophagus and how it works, but the competency requires identifying digestive system parts from pictures/labeled diagrams (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) and describing how they work. The card does not use pictures or diagrams and does not cover the named parts.

copy.en: Muscles in your esophagus squeeze food along in wave-like motions — that's why you can swallow food even upside down!
copy.tl: Ang mga kalamnan sa esophagus ay pumipiga sa pagkain nang paulit-ulit tulad ng alon, kaya nakakalunok ka kahit nakatuwad!
copy.bis: Ang mga kaunuran sa esophagus moduso sa pagkaon sama sa balod, mao nga makalamoy ka bisan nagbaliktad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: boils at about 78 degrees Celsius (78°C)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a boiling point, which is a change of state, but it does not describe melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation, and it does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: boils at about 78 degrees Celsius (78°C)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a specific boiling temperature for ethanol, but it does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state generally, nor does it explain the solid-liquid-gas progression.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: boils at about 78 degrees Celsius (78°C)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a boiling point but does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes.

copy.en: Ethanol, which is a type of alcohol, boils at about 78 degrees Celsius (78°C). It boils at a lower temperature than plain water!
copy.tl: Ang ethanol, na isang uri ng alkohol, ay kumukulo sa mga 78 degrees Celsius (78°C). Kumukulo ito sa mas mababang temperatura kaysa sa tubig!
copy.bis: Ang ethanol, nga matang sa alkohol, mobukal sa mga 78 degrees Celsius (78°C). Mobukal kini sa mas ubos nga temperatura kay sa ordinaryong tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: eat insects
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states shrews eat insects, but the competency requires grouping animals into herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores. The card does not classify shrews into any of these categories nor provide the grouping framework, so it only shares a diet fact without direct instructional support.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: live in our forests
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions shrews live in forests, which is a habitat, but the competency requires using a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants as terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial. The card provides no drawing/diagram and does not explicitly classify the shrew as terrestrial, so it does not directly support the required activity.

copy.en: The Philippines has its own shrews too! Like the Etruscan shrew, Filipino shrews are small, eat insects, and live in our forests.
copy.tl: May sariling shrew din ang Pilipinas! Tulad ng Etruscan shrew, maliliit at kumakain ng insekto ang mga Pilipinong shrew na matatagpuan sa kagubatan.
copy.bis: Ang Pilipinas adunay kaugalingong shrew usab! Sama sa Etruscan shrew, gagmay ug mokaon og insekto ang mga Pilipinhong shrew nga makita sa kalasangan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Europa, one of Jupiter's moons, likely has a huge ocean of liquid water beneath its thick ice crust!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Europa as a moon of Jupiter and a single feature (subsurface ocean), but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name multiple major celestial objects, or discuss their main features and general composition. It is only tangentially related to the solar system topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists think it could harbour microbial life.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about water as a basic need of plants and animals on Earth. The card discusses a possible subsurface ocean on Europa and potential microbial life there, which is not about the basic needs of Earth's plants and animals. The water mentioned is not presented as a need for organisms in the sense of the competency.

copy.en:
Could there be life on Jupiter's moon Europa?

Europa, one of Jupiter's moons, likely has a huge ocean of liquid water beneath its thick ice crust! Scientists think it could harbour microbial life.
copy.tl:
Maaari bang may buhay sa buwan ng Jupiter na Europa?

Ang Europa, isa sa mga buwan ng Jupiter, ay malamang na may malaking ocean ng liquid water sa ilalim ng makapal nitong ice crust! Sa tingin ng mga siyentipiko, maaari itong magkaroon ng microbial life.
copy.bis:
Mahimong adunay kinabuhi sa buwan sa Jupiter nga Europa?

Ang Europa, usa sa mga buwan sa Jupiter, lagmit adunay dako nga ocean sa liquid water sa ubos sa iyang baga nga ice crust! Ang mga syentipiko nagtuo nga mahimong adunay microbial life didto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These areas are called danger zones! People cannot live here to keep them safe from the volcano.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that danger zones exist to keep people safe. It does not involve using local information or reliable sources to identify volcano locations, nor assessing eruption risk to a community, which are the core actions of G6-E-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These areas are called danger zones! People cannot live here to keep them safe from the volcano.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a general safety concept (danger zones) but does not interpret PHIVOLCS alert levels or demonstrate what to do before, during, and after an eruption. No direct instructional support for G6-E-5.

copy.en:
Why are people not allowed to live in certain areas near a volcano?

These areas are called danger zones! People cannot live here to keep them safe from the volcano.
copy.tl:
Bakit bawal manirahan ang mga tao sa ilang lugar malapit sa bulkan?

Ang mga lugar na ito ay tinatawag na danger zones! Bawal manirahan dito para sa kaligtasan ng mga tao.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili tugotan ang mga tawo nga mopuyo sa pipila ka lugar duol sa bulkan?

Kini nga mga lugar gitawag og danger zones! Dili sila pwede mopuyo dinhi para sa kaluwasan sa mga tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Eyes evolved separately many times in different animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents convergent evolution as a concept but does not address the lines of evidence (fossils, biogeography, comparative morphology) that the competency requires. It is a specific example of evolution, not instruction on how evidence supports evolution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Eyes evolved separately many times in different animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on the concept of convergent evolution but does not discuss the listed concepts (variation, heredity, isolation, selection, adaptation) nor the small-group discussion activity. It is only loosely related to the theories of evolution.

copy.en:
Why do octopus and human eyes look alike?

Eyes evolved separately many times in different animals — the octopus eye and a vertebrate eye look similar but developed independently, called convergent evolution.
copy.tl:
Bakit magkatulad ang mata ng octopus at tao?

Ang mga mata ay nag-evolve nang hiwalay sa iba't ibang hayop — magkatulad ang mata ng octopus at ng vertebrate pero magkaiba ang pinanggalingan, tinatawag na convergent evolution.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga managsama ang mata sa octopus ug tawo?

Ang mga mata nag-evolve nga bulag-bulag sa lain-laing hayop — managsama ang mata sa octopus ug sa vertebrate apan lahi ang gigikanan, gitawag og convergent evolution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Evolution has no fixed goal and doesn't always move toward being more complex
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the general direction of evolution, not the specific concepts listed in the competency (variation, heredity, isolation, selection, adaptation). It does not support a discussion of those mechanisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Evolution has no fixed goal and doesn't always move toward being more complex
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card makes a general statement about evolution lacking a goal, but does not describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change. It provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Does evolution have a goal?

No! Evolution has no fixed goal and doesn't always move toward being more complex — it's like a growing bush where some branches stay the same, many die out, and others keep branching.
copy.tl:
May tiyak bang direksyon ang ebolusyon?

Wala! Walang itinatakdang direksyon ang ebolusyon at hindi laging patungo sa mas komplikado — parang ito'y isang lumalagong palumpong kung saan may sangang hindi nagbabago, may namamatay, at may paulit-ulit na nagsasanga.
copy.bis:
Aduna bay tinong direksyon ang ebolusyon?

Wala! Walay tinong direksyon ang ebolusyon ug dili kanunay mopaingon sa mas komplikado — sama kini sa nagtubo nga sapinit diin ang pipila ka sanga wala nagausab, daghan ang mamatay, ug ang uban padayon nga magsanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: are great exercise — you run, jump, and move a lot while playing!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses street games as exercise, mentioning running, jumping, and moving. It does not describe how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Filipino street games like patintero, tumbang preso, and luksong tinik are great exercise — you run, jump, and move a lot while playing!
copy.tl: Ang mga larong-kalye tulad ng patintero, tumbang preso, at luksong tinik ay magandang ehersisyo dahil tumatakbo, tumatalon, at gumagalaw ka nang husto habang naglalaro!
copy.bis: Ang mga dula sa kalye sama sa patintero, tumbang preso, ug luksong tinik maayong ehersisyo kay modagan, molukso, ug molihok ka og maayo samtang nagdula!

copy.en: The more you use your muscles through exercise, the stronger they get!
copy.tl: Kapag madalas mong ginagamit ang iyong mga kalamnan sa ehersisyo, lumalakas ang mga ito!
copy.bis: Kon kanunay nimong gamiton ang imong kaunoran sa ehersisyo, mokusog kini!

copy.en: Steady exercise strengthens our lungs so we can breathe better.
copy.tl: Ang tuloy-tuloy na ehersisyo ay nagpapalakas ng ating mga baga para mas mahusay tayong huminga.
copy.bis: Ang padayon nga ehersisyo nagpakusog sa atong mga baga aron mas maayo tang makaginhawa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an exoplanet passes its star, starlight travels through its atmosphere.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about exoplanet atmospheres and spectroscopy, not about the general structure of the solar system, names of major celestial objects, their features, or composition. Exoplanets are outside the solar system, and the card gives no solar-system content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Analyzing this light's spectrum lets astronomers identify what's inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions analyzing light's spectrum, which relates to electromagnetic radiation, but it does not describe EMR as energy created by vibrations of charged particles or as transverse waves. It only uses the concept of spectroscopy without teaching the required definition or mechanism.

copy.en:
How do scientists know what's in an exoplanet's atmosphere?

When an exoplanet passes its star, starlight travels through its atmosphere. Analyzing this light's spectrum lets astronomers identify what's inside — including possible biosignatures like water and oxygen!
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ang atmosphere ng exoplanet?

Nang dumadaan ang exoplanet sa harap ng bituin, ang liwanag ay dumadaan sa atmosphere nito. Sa pagsusuri ng spectrum, nalalaman ng astronomer ang laman, kasama ang posibleng biosignatures tulad ng tubig at oxygen!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkabalo sa atmosphere sa exoplanet?

Kung ang exoplanet moagi sa atubangan sa bituin, ang kahayag moagi sa atmosphere niini. Sa pag-analyze sa spectrum, makila sa astronomer ang sulod, lakip ang posibleng biosignatures sama sa tubig ug oxygen!

copy.en: The iris has tiny muscles that change the size of your pupil to control how much light gets in!
copy.tl: May maliliit na kalamnan ang iris na nagbabago sa laki ng balintataw para kontrolin ang liwanag!
copy.bis: Ang iris adunay gagmay nga unod nga nagbag-o sa gidak-on sa kalimutaw aron pugngan ang kahayag!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes light-sensing cells in the retina, which is part of the sensory/nervous system. assignedReviews.card_evidence: The retina has two kinds of light-sensing cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts

The card mentions rod and cone cells but does not teach microscope techniques or the listed cell organelles, so it only shares the broad topic of cells.

copy.en: The retina has two kinds of light-sensing cells: rod cells for seeing in dim light, and cone cells for seeing color in bright light.
copy.tl: May dalawang uri ng photoreceptor ang retina: ang rod cells para sa pananaw sa mahinang liwanag, at ang cone cells para sa pagkita ng kulay.
copy.bis: Ang retina adunay duha ka klase sa photoreceptor: ang rod cells alang sa panan-aw sa hanap nga kahayag, ug ang cone cells alang sa pagkita ug kolor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they help steer rainwater away from your eyes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer body part (eyebrows) but describes a role (diverting rain) that is not about movement or gathering food, which are the specific roles required by the competency.

copy.en: Your eyebrows aren't just for looks — they help steer rainwater away from your eyes!
copy.tl: Hindi lang pampaganda ang kilay — tumutulong din itong ipadaplis ang tubig-ulan palayo sa mata!
copy.bis: Dili ra pampaguwapo ang kilay — motabang usab kini sa pagpadaplin sa tubig-ulan palayo sa mata!

copy.en: Eyelashes catch dust and dirt before it can get into your eye!
copy.tl: Ang pilikmata ay sumasalo sa alikabok at dumi bago pa ito makapasok sa mata!
copy.bis: Ang pilok mosalo sa abog ug hugaw sa dili pa kini makasulod sa mata!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses eyes as a body part, but the competency specifically targets outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) and their roles in movement and food gathering. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your eyes help you balance by showing whether you're upright or leaning
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory

It does not describe how any of those systems work, so it provides no direct instructional support.

copy.en:
Why is standing with eyes closed harder?

Your eyes help you balance by showing whether you're upright or leaning — that's why closing them makes standing still much harder!
copy.tl:
Bakit mahirap tumayong nakapikit?

Tumutulong ang mata sa balanse dahil nakikita nito kung tuwid ka o nakatagilid — kaya mas mahirap tumayo nang nakapikit!
copy.bis:
Nganong lisod motindog nga piyong?

Ang imong mata motabang sa balanse kay makita niini kung tul-id ka o nagharag — mao nga mas lisod motindog nga piyong!

copy.tl: Ang tubig ay kumukulo sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!
copy.bis: Ang tubig mobukal sa 212 degrees Fahrenheit (212°F)!

copy.en:
How did the craters on the moon form?

Big space rocks crashed into it long ago! Since the moon has no air to smooth its surface, those crash marks stay there forever.
copy.tl:
Paano nabuo ang mga crater sa buwan?

Tumama ang malalaking batong galing sa kalawakan noong unang panahon! Dahil walang hangin ang buwan para pumantay ito, nananatili ang mga marka!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagporma sa mga crater sa bulan?

Miigo ang dagkong bato gikan sa kawanangan kaniadto! Tungod kay walay hangin ang bulan aron mopatag niini, magpabilin kining mga marka!

copy.en:
Who is the Father of Electricity?

Michael Faraday is often called the Father of Electricity because of his amazing discoveries!
copy.tl:
Sino ang Ama ng Kuryente?

Si Michael Faraday ang madalas tawaging Ama ng Kuryente (Father of Electricity) dahil sa kanyang mga natuklasan!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang Amahan sa Koryente?

Si Michael Faraday kasagaran tawgon nga Amahan sa Koryente (Father of Electricity) tungod sa iyang mga nadiskubrehan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 'Faster spin' means more full turns in the same time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The competency defines speed as how far an object moves in a given time (linear speed, distance/time). It shares the general idea of 'how much happens in a given time' but does not directly teach the concept of speed as distance traveled per time.

copy.en: 'Faster spin' means more full turns in the same time! A wheel spinning twice per second is faster than one spinning just once per second.
copy.tl: Ang 'mas mabilis na pag-ikot' ay mas maraming buong ikot sa parehong oras! Ang gulong na umiikot ng dalawang beses kada segundo ay mas mabilis kaysa sa isang beses.
copy.bis: Ang 'mas paspas nga pagtuyok' nagpasabot og mas daghang tibuok liko sa parehas nga panahon! Ang ligid nga molibot og duha ka beses kada segundo mas paspas kaysa kausa.

copy.en: A drill has a sharp bit that spins very fast to make holes in wood or walls! The faster it spins, the easier it digs in, making the hole quickly.
copy.tl: Ang drill ay may matulis na bahagi na umiikot nang napakabilis para gumawa ng butas sa kahoy o pader! Mas mabilis ang pag-ikot, mas madali itong humukay, kaya mas mabilis matapos.
copy.bis: Ang drill adunay hait nga bahin nga motuyok og paspas kaayo aron makahimo og lungag sa kahoy o bongbong! Kung mas paspas ang pagtuyok, mas sayon mokalot, busa mas paspas mahuman.

copy.tl: Ang pinakamabilis na jet na eroplanong may piloto ay ang SR-71 Blackbird — umaabot ito ng halos 3,500 km/h, mga Mach 3!
copy.bis: Ang pinakapaspas nga jet nga eroplano nga adunay piloto mao ang SR-71 Blackbird — miabot kini ug mga 3,500 km/h, mga Mach 3!

copy.tl: Ang itinuturing na pinakamabilis na tao ay si Usain Bolt mula sa Jamaica!
copy.bis: Ang giila nga pinakatulin nga tawo mao si Usain Bolt gikan sa Jamaica!

What's the fastest land animal on Earth?

The cheetah! It can sprint up to about 100 to 120 kilometers per hour.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabilis na hayop sa lupa?

Ang cheetah! Kaya nitong tumakbo nang hanggang mga 100 hanggang 120 kilometro kada oras.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakapaspas nga mananap sa yuta?

Ang cheetah! Makadagan kini hangtod sa mga 100 ngadto 120 ka kilometro kada oras.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions speed only in the sense of 'fastest', but does not define speed as distance over time, nor discuss distance, time, or measurement. It does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying the definition of speed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nothing travels faster than light!

assignedReviews.reason: The card states that light is the fastest thing, but does not describe electromagnetic radiation as energy created by vibrating charged particles, nor mention transverse waves or travel through materials/space. copy.en: Nothing travels faster than light! It is the absolute fastest thing in the whole universe.
copy.tl: Walang bagay na mas mabilis kaysa sa liwanag! Ito ang pinakamabilis sa buong uniberso.
copy.bis: Walay butang nga mas paspas pa sa kahayag! Kini ang kinapaspasan sa tibuok uniberso.

Who is the Father of Microbiology?

Antonie van Leeuwenhoek! He earned that title for being the very first person to ever see microbes.
copy.tl:
Sino ang Ama ng Mikrobyolohiya?

Si Antonie van Leeuwenhoek! Tinawag siyang Ama ng Mikrobyolohiya dahil siya ang unang nakakita ng mga mikrobyo.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang Amahan sa Microbiology?

Si Antonie van Leeuwenhoek! Gitawag siya nga Amahan sa Microbiology tungod kay siya ang unang nakakita sa mga mikrobyo.

copy.en: Dr. Fe del Mundo earned the title National Scientist of the Philippines for her amazing work in children's health!
